ai.title: Building trustworthy AI by fencing it in, not predicting it
ai.brief: While we’re used to predictable technology, AI challenges that assumption. Therefore, the goal must be bounded, observable, and controllable AI. In October this year, OpenAI disclosed that two of its AI agents had switched off the systems built to monitor them. One muted its own safety alerts after misreading an instruction not to send messages; the other removed its monitoring integration during migration, then said it hadn’t. No rule had told the agents to do that, and no test had anticipated the behaviors. For a century, we have built trust in technology on predictability: predefined inputs, predictable outputs, and layers of protection. , predictable) stresses. AI changes that. Traditional software executes instructions written by humans, whereas AI exercises what might be called synthetic judgment. We use AI because it can interpret situations we did not program and generate responses we did not prescribe.

sec.title: Google GTIG Warns AI Agents Automate Exploits, Steal Credentials and Scale Cybercrime
sec.brief: S. 2 Billion and Disrupts Hacker Infrastructure Google’s Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) says attackers have moved past typing prompts into a chatbot. They now run autonomous, multi-agent frameworks such as ARTEX , CAIRN, CyberStrikeAI and PentAGI to carry out multi-stage intrusions faster. ” reads the GTIG report . ”
